title: Prime Minister urges people to participate in Har Ghar Tiranga movement
body_text:
Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi has called upon citizens to participate enthusiastically in the Har Ghar Tiranga movement and renew their collective resolve to contribute towards building a Viksit Bharat. Shri Modi said that the Tricolour is a symbol of India’s pride and a constant source of inspiration for every citizen to strive to give their best for the nation.
Shri Modi expressed happiness that this year’s Har Ghar Tiranga campaign is dedicated to Vande Mataram, as the nation marks the 150th anniversary of the national song.
The Prime Minister posted on X:
Our Tricolour is our pride and a constant source of inspiration to always give our best for the nation.
Let us participate enthusiastically in the #HarGharTiranga movement and renew our collective resolve to contribute towards building a Viksit Bharat. Glad that this year’s efforts are dedicated to Vande Mataram and that too at a time when we are marking its 150th anniversary.

enrichment.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi urged citizens to actively participate in the Har Ghar Tiranga movement, calling it a step towards realising the vision of a Viksit Bharat. He noted that this year's campaign is dedicated to Vande Mataram, coinciding with the 150th anniversary of the national song. The appeal was made via a post on X, along with a link to the official Har Ghar Tiranga website.
enrichment.context: The Har Ghar Tiranga campaign was launched in 2022 as part of the Azadi Ka Amrit Mahotsav commemorations marking 75 years of India's independence, encouraging citizens to hoist the national flag at their homes to foster a sense of patriotism and personal connection with the Tricolour. The campaign has since become an annual feature around Independence Day, reflecting the government's broader strategy of using symbolic and participatory public campaigns to build national consciousness. This year's dedication to Vande Mataram is significant because 2026 marks 150 years since Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay composed the song (published in 1882 as part of the novel Anandamath), which played a pivotal role in inspiring the freedom movement and was later adopted as India's National Song. Linking the flag campaign to Vande Mataram's anniversary underscores the government's emphasis on connecting contemporary nation-building initiatives with India's freedom struggle heritage, a recurring theme in commemorative programming tied to national identity and civic participation.

prelims_questions.question:
With reference to 'Vande Mataram', consider the following statements:
1. It was composed by Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay.
2. It was first published as part of the novel 'Anandamath'.
3. It has the same constitutional status as the National Anthem.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
prelims_questions.explanation: Vande Mataram was composed by Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay and first appeared in his novel Anandamath. However, it holds the status of 'National Song', which is distinct from the 'National Anthem' (Jana Gana Mana); the two do not have identical constitutional status, hence statement 3 is incorrect.

prelims_questions.question: The 'Har Ghar Tiranga' campaign was launched as part of which broader commemorative initiative of the Government of India?
prelims_questions.explanation: The Har Ghar Tiranga campaign was launched in 2022 under the Azadi Ka Amrit Mahotsav, commemorating 75 years of India's independence, to encourage citizens to hoist the national flag at their homes.

mains_questions.question: Discuss the significance of national symbols such as the Tricolour and the National Song in fostering a sense of collective identity and nationalism among citizens. In this context, examine the role of government-led mass participation campaigns like Har Ghar Tiranga.
'Vande Mataram' played a crucial role in inspiring India's freedom struggle. Trace its historical evolution and discuss its continuing relevance in contemporary nation-building narratives.
